passages.text: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the Christian brothers in Corinth.
Paul reminds them about the gospel.
Paul preached this gospel to them.
They received this gospel from Paul.
They now stand firm in this gospel.
passages.original: Γνωρίζω δὲ ὑμῖν ἀδελφοί τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε ἐν ᾧ καὶ ἑστήκατε

passages.text: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the brothers in Corinth.
Paul preached the gospel to them.
This gospel saves them.
They must hold firmly to the word Paul preached.
If they do not hold firmly, their belief is empty.
If they do not hold firmly, their faith is useless.
passages.original: δι’ οὗ καὶ σῴζεσθε τίνι λόγῳ εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν εἰ κατέχετε ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε

passages.text: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures, and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthian Christians.
Paul received a message of first importance.
Paul passed this message on to the Corinthians.
Christ died for our sins.
The Scriptures foretold this.
Christ was buried.
God raised Christ on the third day.
The Scriptures foretold this.
Christ appeared to Cephas.
Christ then appeared to the Twelve apostles.
passages.original: Παρέδωκα γὰρ ὑμῖν ἐν πρώτοις ὃ καὶ παρέλαβον ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν κατὰ τὰς γραφάς καὶ ὅτι ἐτάφη καὶ ὅτι ἐγήγερται τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ κατὰ τὰς γραφάς καὶ ὅτι ὤφθη Κηφᾷ εἶτα τοῖς δώδεκα

passages.text: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
passages.sermon: Jesus appeared to more than five hundred believers at one time.\r\nMost of these believers are still alive now.\r\nSome of these believers have died.
passages.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐφάπαξ ἐξ ὧν οἱ πλείονες μένουσιν ἕως ἄρτι τινὲς δὲ ἐκοιμήθησαν

passages.text: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
passages.sermon: Jesus appeared to James.\r\nThen Jesus appeared to all the apostles.
passages.original: ἔπειτα ὤφθη Ἰακώβῳ εἶτα τοῖς ἀποστόλοις πᾶσιν

passages.text: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.
passages.sermon:
Jesus appeared to me last of all.
He appeared to me after He appeared to the others.
I am like one born at the wrong time.
Jesus showed Himself to me, even though I was not like the others.
passages.original: ἔσχατον δὲ πάντων ὡσπερεὶ τῷ ἐκτρώματι ὤφθη κἀμοί

passages.text: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is an apostle.
Paul says he is the least of the apostles.
Paul says he is not worthy to be called an apostle.
Paul persecuted the church of God.
passages.original: Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι ὁ ἐλάχιστος τῶν ἀποστόλων ὃς οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς καλεῖσθαι ἀπόστολος διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
passages.sermon:
God showed me grace.
God’s grace made me who I am.
God’s grace to me was not empty.
God’s grace changed me.
I worked harder than all the other apostles.
But it was not really me who did this.
God’s grace worked with me.
passages.original: χάριτι δὲ Θεοῦ εἰμι ὅ εἰμι καὶ ἡ χάρις αὐτοῦ ἡ εἰς ἐμὲ οὐ κενὴ ἐγενήθη ἀλλὰ περισσότερον αὐτῶν πάντων ἐκοπίασα οὐκ ἐγὼ δὲ ἀλλὰ ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ σὺν ἐμοί

passages.text: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Other apostles also preach about Jesus Christ.
Paul and the other apostles preach the same message.
This is the message you heard.
You believed this message.
passages.original: εἴτε οὖν ἐγὼ εἴτε ἐκεῖνοι οὕτως κηρύσσομεν καὶ οὕτως ἐπιστεύσατε

passages.text: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and others preach that God raised Christ from the dead.
Some people among you say there is no resurrection of the dead.
If we preach that Christ was raised from the dead, this message is clear.
How can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς κηρύσσεται ὅτι ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγήγερται πῶς λέγουσιν ἐν ὑμῖν τινες ὅτι ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul teaches about the resurrection of the dead.
If God does not raise the dead, then Christ has not been raised.
If there is no resurrection, Christ did not rise from the dead.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν οὐκ ἔστιν οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται

passages.text: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul teaches about the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
If God did not raise Christ from the dead, then Christ is still dead.
If Christ is still dead, our preaching has no value.
If Christ is still dead, your faith has no value.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται κενὸν ἄρα καὶ τὸ κήρυγμα ἡμῶν κενὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν

passages.text: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul and the other apostles preach about God.
They say that God raised Jesus Christ from the dead.
If the dead are not raised, then God did not raise Christ.
If God did not raise Christ, then Paul and the other apostles are false witnesses about God.
They are found to be false witnesses because they testified that God raised Christ.
This testimony would be false if the dead are not raised.
passages.original: εὑρισκόμεθα δὲ καὶ ψευδομάρτυρες τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι ἐμαρτυρήσαμεν κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι ἤγειρεν τὸν Χριστόν ὃν οὐκ ἤγειρεν εἴπερ ἄρα νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται

passages.text: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul teaches about the resurrection of the dead.
If God does not raise dead people, then no dead person rises.
If God does not raise dead people, then Christ did not rise from the dead.
If the dead are not raised, then Christ has not been raised.
passages.original: Εἰ γὰρ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται οὐδὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται

passages.text: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
If God did not raise Christ from the dead, then Christ is still dead.
If Christ is still dead, your faith does nothing.
Your faith cannot save you.
You are still guilty of your sins.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ Χριστὸς οὐκ ἐγήγερται ματαία ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν ἐστίν ἔτι ἐστὲ ἐν ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth.
He teaches about the resurrection of the dead.
He says some people have died as believers in Christ.
If Christ has not been raised, these believers have perished.
Their hope is lost if there is no resurrection.
passages.original: ἄρα καὶ οἱ κοιμηθέντες ἐν Χριστῷ ἀπώλοντο

passages.text: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Corinthians about faith in Jesus Christ.
Paul says, "If we hope in Christ only for this life, we are to be pitied."
Our hope in Christ must be for more than this life.
If we trust Christ only for earthly things, we are worse off than all people.
People should pity us if our hope in Christ is only for now.
True hope in Christ includes eternal life.
passages.original: εἰ ἐν τῇ ζωῇ ταύτῃ ἐν Χριστῷ ἠλπικότες ἐσμὲν μόνον ἐλεεινότεροι πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐσμέν

passages.text: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
passages.sermon:
Christ is the Son of God.
God raised Christ from the dead.
Christ was dead, but now He lives again.
Christ is the first to rise from the dead.
Many people have died believing in Christ.
Christ is the firstfruits of those who have died in faith.
Christ’s resurrection shows that others who died in Christ will also rise.
passages.original: Νυνὶ δὲ Χριστὸς ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀπαρχὴ τῶν κεκοιμημένων

passages.text: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
passages.sermon:
Death entered the world through a man named Adam.
Adam was the first man.
Because of Adam, all people die.
Resurrection from the dead also comes through a man.
This man is Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ brings resurrection to all who belong to Him.
passages.original: ἐπειδὴ γὰρ δι’ ἀνθρώπου θάνατος καὶ δι’ ἀνθρώπου ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν

passages.text: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam brought death to all people.
All people die because of Adam.
Christ is the Son of God.
Christ brings life to all people.
All people will be made alive in Christ.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Ἀδὰμ πάντες ἀποθνήσκουσιν οὕτως καὶ ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ πάντες ζωοποιηθήσονται

passages.text: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.
passages.sermon:
Each person will be raised in a certain order.
Christ was raised first.
He is the firstfruits.
When Christ comes again, He will raise those who belong to Him.
passages.original: Ἕκαστος δὲ ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι ἀπαρχὴ Χριστός ἔπειτα οἱ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐν τῇ παρουσίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ will bring the end.
He will give the kingdom to God the Father.
He will do this after He destroys every dominion.
He will destroy every authority.
He will destroy every power.
passages.original: εἶτα τὸ τέλος ὅταν παραδιδῷ τὴν βασιλείαν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί ὅταν καταργήσῃ πᾶσαν ἀρχὴν καὶ πᾶσαν ἐξουσίαν καὶ δύναμιν

passages.text: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
God has given Jesus authority to reign.
Jesus must continue to reign.
He will reign until He defeats all His enemies.
He will put every enemy under His feet.
passages.original: δεῖ γὰρ αὐτὸν βασιλεύειν ἄχρι οὗ θῇ πάντας τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
passages.sermon:
Death is an enemy.
Death is the last enemy.
God will destroy death.
Death will be destroyed at the end.
passages.original: ἔσχατος ἐχθρὸς καταργεῖται ὁ θάνατος

passages.text: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.
passages.sermon:
God put everything under the authority of Jesus.
God made all things subject to Jesus.
The statement says, “Everything has been put under Him.”
This statement does not include God Himself.
God is the One who put everything under Jesus.
God is not subject to Jesus.
God remains above all.
passages.original: Πάντα γὰρ Ὑπέταξεν ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὅταν δὲ εἴπῃ ὅτι πάντα ὑποτέτακται δῆλον ὅτι ἐκτὸς τοῦ ὑποτάξαντος αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα

passages.text: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.
passages.sermon:
God put all things under the authority of the Son.
When God finishes subjecting everything to the Son, this will happen.
The Son Himself will then become subject to God.
God is the One who put all things under the Son.
God will then be all in all.
passages.original: ὅταν δὲ ὑποταγῇ αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Υἱὸς ὑποταγήσεται τῷ ὑποτάξαντι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ἵνα ᾖ ὁ Θεὸς τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν

passages.text: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
passages.sermon:
Some people are baptized for the dead.
They do this because they believe in resurrection.
If the dead are not raised, their action has no purpose.
If there is no resurrection, baptism for the dead is meaningless.
There is no reason to be baptized for the dead if the dead do not rise.
passages.original: Ἐπεὶ τί ποιήσουσιν οἱ βαπτιζόμενοι ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν εἰ ὅλως νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται τί καὶ βαπτίζονται ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν

passages.text: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?
passages.sermon: We are Christians.\r\nWe face danger every hour.\r\nWhy do we risk our lives all the time?
passages.original: τί καὶ ἡμεῖς κινδυνεύομεν πᾶσαν ὥραν

passages.text: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
Paul faces danger every day.
Paul risks his life daily.
Paul calls the believers his brothers.
Paul boasts about the believers.
Paul boasts in Christ Jesus.
Christ Jesus is our Lord.
Paul’s confidence is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
passages.original: καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω νὴ τὴν ὑμετέραν καύχησιν ἀδελφοί ἣν ἔχω ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν

passages.text: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul sometimes faced great danger.
Paul once fought wild beasts in Ephesus.
If Paul did this only for human reasons, he gained nothing.
If God does not raise the dead, there is no hope after death.
If there is no resurrection, people may say, “Let us eat and drink.”
They may say this because tomorrow we die.
passages.original: εἰ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ τί μοι τὸ ὄφελος εἰ νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται Φάγωμεν καὶ πίωμεν αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνήσκομεν

passages.text: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul warns the believers.
Do not let anyone deceive you.
Bad company corrupts good character.
passages.original: Μὴ πλανᾶσθε Φθείρουσιν ἤθη χρηστὰ ὁμιλίαι κακαί

passages.text: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
\r\nPaul urges the believers to wake up and live rightly.
\r\nPaul commands them to stop sinning.
\r\nSome people among them do not know God.
\r\nPaul says this to make them feel ashamed.
passages.original: ἐκνήψατε δικαίως καὶ μὴ ἁμαρτάνετε ἀγνωσίαν γὰρ Θεοῦ τινες ἔχουσιν πρὸς ἐντροπὴν ὑμῖν λαλῶ

passages.text: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul teaches about the resurrection of the dead.
Someone may ask a question.
The question is: How are the dead raised?
The question continues: With what kind of body do the dead come?
passages.original: Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται

passages.text: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to someone who doubts the resurrection of the dead.
Paul calls this person a fool.
A seed must die before it can come to life.
What you sow does not live unless it first dies.
passages.original: ἄφρων σὺ ὃ σπείρεις οὐ ζωοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ

passages.text: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
passages.sermon:
You do not sow the body that will come later.
You sow only a bare seed.
This seed might be wheat.
It might be some other kind of seed.
passages.original: καὶ ὃ σπείρεις οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν

passages.text: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.
passages.sermon:
God acts with purpose and power.
God gives each seed a body.
God chooses the body for each seed.
God gives each kind of seed its own unique body.
God decides how each body will be.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς δίδωσιν αὐτῷ σῶμα καθὼς ἠθέλησεν καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπερμάτων ἴδιον σῶμα

passages.text: Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.
passages.sermon:
Flesh is not all the same.
People have one kind of flesh.
Animals have a different kind of flesh.
Birds have another kind of flesh.
Fish have a different kind of flesh.
passages.original: Οὐ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἡ αὐτὴ σάρξ ἀλλὰ ἄλλη μὲν ἀνθρώπων ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων

passages.text: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.
passages.sermon:
There are heavenly bodies.
There are earthly bodies.
Heavenly bodies have one kind of splendor.
Earthly bodies have a different kind of splendor.
passages.original: καὶ σώματα ἐπουράνια καὶ σώματα ἐπίγεια ἀλλὰ ἑτέρα μὲν ἡ τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξα ἑτέρα δὲ ἡ τῶν ἐπιγείων

passages.text: The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.
passages.sermon:
The sun has its own splendor.
The moon has a different splendor.
The stars have another kind of splendor.
One star differs from another star in splendor.
passages.original: ἄλλη δόξα ἡλίου καὶ ἄλλη δόξα σελήνης καὶ ἄλλη δόξα ἀστέρων ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ

passages.text: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.
passages.sermon: The resurrection of the dead will happen in this way.\r\nPeople bury the body in a perishable state.\r\nGod raises the body in an imperishable state.
passages.original: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν σπείρεται ἐν φθορᾷ ἐγείρεται ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ

passages.text: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks about the resurrection of the dead.
He says the body is sown in dishonor.
God raises it in glory.
The body is sown in weakness.
God raises it in power.
passages.original: σπείρεται ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ σπείρεται ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ ἐγείρεται ἐν δυνάμει

passages.text: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
passages.sermon:
Paul teaches about the resurrection of the dead.
A person is buried with a natural body.
God raises that person with a spiritual body.
A natural body exists.
A spiritual body also exists.
passages.original: σπείρεται σῶμα ψυχικόν ἐγείρεται σῶμα πνευματικόν Εἰ ἔστιν σῶμα ψυχικόν ἔστιν καὶ πνευματικόν

passages.text: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being;” the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
passages.sermon:
The Bible says this.
Adam was the first man.
Adam became a living being.
Jesus is the last Adam.
Jesus became a life-giving spirit.
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ γέγραπται Ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζωοποιοῦν

passages.text: The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
passages.sermon:
The natural body comes first.
The spiritual body comes after the natural body.
The spiritual does not come before the natural.
The natural comes before the spiritual.
passages.original: Ἀλλ’ οὐ πρῶτον τὸ πνευματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ψυχικόν ἔπειτα τὸ πνευματικόν

passages.text: The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam came from the dust of the earth.
Jesus is the second man.
Jesus came from heaven.
passages.original: ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός ὁ δεύτερος ἄνθρωπος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
passages.sermon:
The first man was earthly.
He came from the dust of the earth.
People who belong to the earth are like the earthly man.
The second man is heavenly.
He came from heaven.
People who belong to heaven are like the heavenly man.
passages.original: οἷος ὁ χοϊκός τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι

passages.text: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.
passages.sermon:
Adam was the first man.
Adam was made from the dust of the earth.
We have carried the image of Adam.
We have carried the image of the man from the earth.
Jesus is the second man.
Jesus came from heaven.
We will also carry the image of Jesus.
We will carry the image of the man from heaven.
passages.original: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου

passages.text: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers.
He calls them brothers.
He makes a declaration.
Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God.
The perishable cannot inherit the imperishable.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δέ φημι ἀδελφοί ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν Θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ δύναται οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ

passages.text: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed— in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Christian brothers and sisters.
Paul says he will tell them a mystery.
Not all of us will die.
All of us will be changed.
This change will happen instantly.
It will happen in a moment.
It will be as quick as the blink of an eye.
This will happen at the last trumpet.
The trumpet will sound.
The dead will be raised.
The dead will be raised with bodies that cannot decay.
We who are alive will also be changed.
passages.original: Ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα ἐν ἀτόμῳ ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι σαλπίσει γάρ καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα

passages.text: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
passages.sermon:
People have bodies that can decay.
These bodies are perishable.
People are also mortal.
Perishable bodies cannot last forever.
Mortal people cannot live forever by themselves.
God must change these bodies.
God will clothe the perishable with the imperishable.
God will clothe the mortal with immortality.
Then people will have bodies that do not decay.
Then people will have life that does not end.
passages.original: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν

passages.text: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
passages.sermon:
God will change us.
God will clothe what is perishable with what cannot perish.
God will clothe what is mortal with immortality.
When this happens, a promise will be fulfilled.
The promise is written in Scripture.
The promise says: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος

passages.text: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”
passages.sermon:
Death is a powerful enemy.
Death once claimed victory over people.
Death once brought pain and fear.
Now, death has lost its victory.
Now, death has lost its sting.
passages.original: Ποῦ σου θάνατε τὸ νῖκος ποῦ σου θάνατε τὸ κέντρον

passages.text: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
passages.sermon: Sin is the sting of death.\r\nThe law gives sin its power.
passages.original: Τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος

passages.text: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
passages.sermon: God gives us victory.\r\nGod gives this victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.\r\nWe thank God for this gift.
passages.original: τῷ δὲ Θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to Christians in Corinth.
He calls them his beloved brothers.
He tells them to be steadfast.
He tells them to be immovable.
He tells them to always excel in the work of the Lord.
He reminds them that their labor in the Lord is not in vain.
passages.original: Ὥστε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί ἑδραῖοι γίνεσθε ἀμετακίνητοι περισσεύοντες ἐν τῷ ἔργῳ τοῦ Κυρίου πάντοτε εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κόπος ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔστιν κενὸς ἐν Κυρίῳ
